info.description:
Run a proxy reselling business on HypeProxies from your own systems.

**How reselling works.** You prepay a wallet with us and buy dedicated /24s or IP plans from it
at your reseller prices, in the dashboard or with this API. You split each one into proxy logins
for your own customers with sub-users, and charge your customers on your own store and your own
Stripe account: we never see or touch your customers' payments. Every /24 and plan renews
monthly from your wallet automatically, so keep it funded.

**Base URL.** Every path below starts at `https://app.hypeproxies.com/api`, for example
`https://app.hypeproxies.com/api/v1/reseller/prices`.

**Authentication.** Create an API key in the dashboard under API keys and send it as
`Authorization: ApiKey <key>`. A key acts for the workspace it belongs to. Keys with only the
`read` scope can look but not buy or change anything; keys can also expire and be limited to
your servers' IPs. A full-access key spends the workspace wallet, so keep it on your servers
only. Adding credits to the wallet is done in the dashboard, not through this API.

**Getting started.**
1. `GET /v1/reseller` shows whether the workspace is an approved reseller, and
`GET /v1/reseller/wallet` what the wallet holds and which services renew from it next.
2. `GET /v1/reseller/prices` and `GET /v1/reseller/inventory` show your price list and what
can be bought now, per carrier and physical site (`ashburn-va`); an order may name a site.
3. `POST /v1/reseller/orders` with an `Idempotency-Key` header buys a dedicated /24 or a plan
from the workspace wallet. Retrying with the same key never buys twice. An order the wallet
cannot cover is refused with 409 `Insufficient wallet balance` and takes nothing.
4. `GET /v1/reseller/services` lists what you bought. A service is ready to hand out once its
`ready` is true, usually within a minute.
5. Split a service between your customers with sub-users:
`POST /v1/reseller/services/{service_id}/subusers` creates a proxy login on some of the
service's IPs (`ip_count`, or a list of `ips`) and returns its username, password and proxies.
`GET /v1/reseller/services/{service_id}/subusers` lists them. Each sub-user can be suspended
and resumed, given other IPs, whitelisted by client IP and have its password rotated, so you
cut one customer off without touching the others.
6. Or let us find the IPs: `POST /v1/reseller/packs` with an `Idempotency-Key` header and
`ips`, `label` and `use_case` (and optionally `carrier`, `site`, `whitelists`,
`max_total_cents`) gives one customer a sub-user of that many IPs that no other sub-user
serves. When one of your working /24s or plans has enough spare IPs, it is carved from them at
once (201, with the sub-user and its password). Otherwise the smallest plan that fits (25, 50,
100 or 250 IPs) is bought from the wallet (202, `pending`); the sub-user is created as soon as
the plan is provisioned and `pack.ready` is sent, or `pack.failed` with the reason. Read it
with `GET /v1/reseller/packs/{pack_id}`. A plan bought this way is yours: it renews monthly
and its spare IPs serve your next packs. A pack is refused, and nothing charged, when the
wallet, stock or your `max_total_cents` cannot cover the plan or a whitelisted client IP is
already in use. A pack can still fail after its plan was bought (`pack.failed`): when the plan
is not ready within a day, or a whitelisted client IP or the plan's IPs were taken meanwhile;
the plan stays yours and its IPs serve your next pack.
7. Or hand a whole service to one customer: label it with your customer's name and your own
reference with `PATCH /v1/reseller/services/{service_id}` (find it again with `?reference=`),
read its proxies with `GET /v1/service/proxy/{instance_id}/list`, and change its password with
`PUT /v1/service/proxy/{instance_id}/credentials`.

**Errors.** A refused call answers with its status and `{"error": "<reason>"}`. Refusals your
code may want to handle also carry a stable `code`; match on it, not on the text:
- `insufficient_balance` (409): the wallet cannot cover an order, or a pack's plan. Add
credits in the dashboard.
- `out_of_stock` (409): no carrier on offer has stock for an order that names no carrier.
Try again later, or order less.
- `subuser_limit` (409): the service already has the most sub-users it can have (254).

**Webhooks.** Instead of polling, register an HTTPS endpoint with `POST /v1/reseller/webhooks`.
We post a JSON event to it whenever an order completes, a service is provisioned, suspended,
resumed or ended, a sub-user is created, updated or deleted, a pack is ready or failed, or the
wallet runs low or is reloaded. The answer carries the endpoint's signing secret, shown once. Every request has a
`HypeProxies-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` header: compute HMAC-SHA256 of
`<t>.<raw body>` with the secret, compare it to `v1` in constant time, and reject a `t` more
than five minutes old. Answer with any 2xx within 15 seconds. A failed delivery is retried
for 24 hours, so drop duplicates by the event `id`. Events about one object (its `object`)
arrive in order, numbered by `sequence`; a failing event holds back later events of that
object only. An endpoint that fails every delivery for 24 hours is disabled and the
workspace owner emailed; enabling it again sends the events it missed.

**Example: a first order and a sub-user with curl.** Keep the `Idempotency-Key` with your own
order record and send the same one if you retry.

```sh
export HP_KEY=...   # your API key
curl -X POST "https://app.hypeproxies.com/api/v1/reseller/orders" \
  -H "Authorization: ApiKey $HP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 7d4c3c1e-5b8a-4b8e-9a51-0c6a2e1d9f10" \
  -d '{"type": "plan", "ips": 25, "use_case": "retail"}'
# The answer lists the new service in "services". Once GET /v1/reseller/services shows
# it "ready" (usually within a minute), give one of your customers 5 of its IPs:
export SERVICE_ID=...   # from the order's "services"
curl -X POST "https://app.hypeproxies.com/api/v1/reseller/services/$SERVICE_ID/subusers" \
  -H "Authorization: ApiKey $HP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"label": "Customer 1042", "reference": "cus_1042", "ip_count": 5}'
```

**Example: the same in Node.js (18 or later).**

```js
import crypto from "node:crypto";

const base = "https://app.hypeproxies.com/api";
async function call(path, init = {}) {
  const response = await fetch(base + path, {
    ...init,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `ApiKey ${process.env.HP_KEY}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...init.headers,
    },
  });
  const body = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${response.status} ${body.error}`);
  return body;
}

// Store the key with your order and reuse it on a retry: it never buys twice.
const order = await call("/v1/reseller/orders", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Idempotency-Key": crypto.randomUUID() },
  body: JSON.stringify({ type: "plan", ips: 25, use_case: "retail" }),
});
// Wait until the new service is provisioned, usually within a minute.
const serviceId = order.services[0];
for (let ready = false; !ready; ) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5000));
  const { services } = await call("/v1/reseller/services");
  ready = services.some((service) => service.service_id === serviceId && service.ready);
}
// Split it for a customer: a login on 5 of its IPs.
const subuser = await call(`/v1/reseller/services/${serviceId}/subusers`, {
  method: "POST",
  body: JSON.stringify({ label: "Customer 1042", reference: "cus_1042", ip_count: 5 }),
});
console.log(subuser.username, subuser.password, subuser.proxies);
```

**Example: checking a webhook's signature in Node.js.** Pass the body exactly as received,
before any JSON parsing.

```js
import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verifySignature(rawBody, header, secret) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(",").map((part) => part.split("=")));
  const sentAt = Number(parts.t);
  if (!Number.isInteger(sentAt) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - sentAt) > 300) return false;
  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${parts.t}.`)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest();
  const given = Buffer.from(parts.v1 ?? "", "hex");
  return given.length === expected.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
}
```

Apply to resell for the current workspace. The workspace owner then verifies their
identity (`POST /reseller/identity`), which activates the application; staff can also
decide it themselves.

# Errors
Returns validation errors, `Forbidden` for plain members and `Conflict` if the
workspace already has an application that was not rejected.

Start or resume the workspace owner's identity verification (ID document and matching
selfie, through Stripe Identity). Open the returned URL right away: it works once.

# Errors
`Forbidden` for anyone but the workspace owner, `NotFound` before applying, `Conflict` when
there is nothing to verify, `ServiceUnavailable` when Stripe cannot be reached.

# Errors

post.description:
Buy dedicated /24s or a pay-as-you-go plan from the workspace wallet, at the
reseller price list. Send a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (UUID) per order: a retry
with the same key returns the first answer and never charges twice.

# Errors
Returns `BadRequest` for a missing key, bad order, or unknown carrier or site, `Forbidden`
unless an owner or admin of an approved reseller, and `Conflict` when prices are
not set, stock or the wallet is short, or the key was used for another order.

A customer's sub-user of `ips` IPs that no other sub-user serves. It is carved at once from
spare IPs of one of the workspace's working /24s or plans that match the carrier, site and
use case (`201`, with the sub-user and its password). When none has room, the smallest
pay-as-you-go plan that fits is bought from the wallet (`202`, `pending`); the sub-user is
created as soon as the plan is provisioned, `pack.ready` is sent, and this pack shows it.
A plan bought for a pack stays and renews; its spare IPs serve later packs.

Send a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (UUID) per pack: a retry with the same key returns the same
pack (`200`) and never charges or creates twice.

# Errors
Returns `BadRequest` for a missing key, a bad pack, or an unknown carrier or site,
`Forbidden` unless an owner or admin of an approved reseller, `Conflict` when the key was
used for another pack, a whitelisted client IP is already in use in the workspace, prices
are not set or stock or the wallet is short, and `ServiceUnavailable` when our proxy
servers did not take the sub-user. Nothing is charged or created on an error.

post.description:
Swaps some of the proxy service's IPs for new ones of the same kind. Each IP sent must
be one of the service's. The new IPs work as soon as the call returns.

# Errors

Returns:
- `NotFound` for a proxy service that is not the workspace's or is not set up yet.
- `BadRequest` for an empty list, an IP that is not the service's, a `reason` that is
  empty or over 500 characters, or when there are not enough free IPs to replace them with.
- `TooManyRequests` while the cooldown after the last replacement runs.
- `Conflict` when the service's IPs changed or were resynced during the replacement,
  which replaces nothing.
- `ServiceUnavailable` when our proxy servers did not confirm the new IPs in time. Any
  other error from our proxy servers comes back with its own status, usually a 5xx.

400.description: Invalid IPs or no replacement capacity

409.description: The service's IPs changed or were resynced during the replacement

503.description: Proxy servers did not confirm in time
